reviews.decision: The test-target composition module owns explicit links for the complete unit, MPI, and public-header matrix; its dependency count is the test topology and is isolated from production and package target ownership.

The snapshot contract keeps header compatibility, single-rank identity validation, and immutable SoA frame validation together so an IO writer receives one preflighted value boundary; serialization, disk access, and distributed shards remain outside this header.

The lifecycle adapter keeps runtime initialization, external ownership, and process-exit finalization together; collectives, packet operations, and ghost requests are split into separate native units.
The ghost adapter combines platform guards with request validation and cancellation so MPI request lifetime is closed in one native boundary; transport orchestration remains outside the file.
The C ABI fixture keeps one end-to-end lifecycle scenario so ABI ordering and cleanup remain visible; its length is registered for review rather than hidden from the repository report.

The bounded-view fixture validates related invalid-input cases and the split SDK contracts in one contract scenario; its length and include dependencies are tracked and remain outside production code.
The contract fixture groups the public and internal invariant checks needed to detect drift across the SDK boundary; the review signal remains explicit.
The dynamics fixture keeps deterministic physical cases together so shared setup and comparison rules cannot diverge; the signal is registered for later focused decomposition.
The hierarchy fixture compares tree construction and solver behavior in one deterministic scenario; its test-only function length is visible and reviewed.
The lifecycle fixture intentionally exercises construction, mutation, failure, and cleanup in sequence; the signal is accepted as a test-harness responsibility review.

The architecture gate keeps one five-argument file-analysis boundary so profile thresholds and exception handling are applied consistently; the signal is registered and does not waive production thresholds.
The callable scanner handles C++ lexical edge cases and explicit exceptions in one validator; its branching is tool-local and remains covered by its fixture suite.
The formatter implements the repository's scope-sensitive grouping grammar and recursive statement handling; the current complexity is exposed for a later tool decomposition instead of ignored.
The frozen-plan gate validates mutually dependent manifest, roots, phase, CTest, naming, and forbidden-reference contracts; its signal is registered while the gate remains a single policy boundary.

The naming report materializes separate collision, exception, length, type-mapping, and responsibility result lists so CI can distinguish each contract failure; allocation and branching are limited to deterministic policy-report construction.

The public boundary gate keeps include, pointer, fixed-width ABI, internal-facade, and parameter-exception checks in one diagnostic boundary so a public contract violation reports its owning rule and source line.

The capability gate keeps matrix validation, deferred-root checks, and public unsupported-status checks in one policy boundary so compile claims cannot drift from the frozen plan; its tool-local signals are covered by the fixture and do not waive production thresholds.

The scaling CLI keeps option parsing and stable record emission together so every workload invocation has the same machine-readable fields; its branching is test-harness local and is covered by the evidence runner fixtures.

The pure contract module validates and expands one versioned workload schema and parses rank records; its report-list allocations and validation branches are policy-local, deterministic, and covered by release_evidence_test.py.

The evidence runner keeps command execution, rank validation, capability metadata, and external artifact publication in one benchmark boundary; its branching is the explicit state policy for passed, failed, skipped, and unknown evidence.

The HDF5 evidence runner keeps contract validation, backend record parsing, and enabled/unavailable qualification in one deterministic evidence boundary; its branching is policy validation covered by dedicated fixtures.

Migration retains one collective transaction boundary so every early return records the same diagnostic status and clears received packets consistently; packet preparation and exchange remain split into dedicated methods.

Run configuration keeps directive dispatch, duplicate detection, required-field validation, and candidate commit together so parsing failures cannot mutate the caller's configuration; value policies are split into dedicated adapters.

The output directive keeps binary defaulting, optional HDF5 format parsing, path validation, and candidate configuration assignment in one bounded semantic adapter; the format is internal and the capability check remains at output preparation.

The added rank, local-count, overlap, and migration accessors form one observability boundary for the internal qualification harness; they do not widen the public SDK ABI or add simulation responsibilities.

The reader keeps bounded file loading, header and payload preflight, checksum and EOF verification, and transactional decode in one persistence boundary; fixed wire parsing is delegated to SnapshotWire and the read path is bounded by the frozen snapshot contract.

The HDF5 reader keeps schema validation, bounded staging, checksum verification, and transactional commit in one adapter boundary; the public snapshot contract remains independent of the optional backend.

Manifest validation and atomic publication remain one metadata contract: validation covers the complete persisted configuration before any file is opened, while the fixed-order writer delegates JSON field emission to MetadataManifestJson.cpp.

The run boundary keeps preparation, ordered local shard publication, root manifest commit, rollback, and path observability together; the publication state machine is shared by binary and HDF5 adapters without duplicating distributed coordination.

The CLI run entrypoint keeps topology preflight, simulation setup, non-collective local capture, collective status handling, checkpoint execution, and summary publication together as one orchestration boundary; shard persistence is delegated to the output and metadata boundaries.

The CLI output boundary keeps topology validation, collective status synchronization, local atomic shard publication, root manifest commit, and online conservation publication together so all ranks follow one checkpoint state machine; post-processing consumes the explicit shard contract without duplicating the simulation loop.

Input validation keeps manifest compatibility, deterministic step checks, exact state-directory inventory, and snapshot-frame preflight in one persistence boundary; it rejects invalid runs before post-processing output is created.

The end-to-end test keeps artifact preparation and rejection cases in one fixture boundary so the production CLI, direct API path, atomic output behavior, and online byte-parity contract are verified together.

The contract validator keeps ownership, lane, and historical issue schema checks together so the final audit cannot run against a partial plan; its branching is policy validation and is covered by audit_test.py.

The layout contract validator keeps the frozen candidate matrix, typed record parsing, and cross-representation hash invariants together; its allocations and branches construct validation diagnostics only and are covered by layout_evidence_test.py.

The layout evidence runner keeps executable discovery, external artifact publication, and strict matrix qualification in one evidence boundary; its branches distinguish contract, process, and record failures and are covered by layout_evidence_test.py.

The reduction benchmark keeps deterministic cancellation construction, policy timing, and the long-run KDK probe in one qualification boundary; the production reduction and conservation contracts remain separate, and the runner validates the complete result matrix.

The reduction contract validator keeps candidate selection, typed record parsing, and cross-policy invariants together; its allocations and branches only build validation diagnostics and are covered by reduction_evidence_test.py.

The reduction evidence runner keeps executable discovery, external artifact publication, and strict matrix qualification in one evidence boundary; its branches distinguish contract, process, and record failures and are covered by reduction_evidence_test.py.

The grid query boundary keeps the bounded 27-cell traversal, hash-collision lookup, radius filtering, and deterministic per-target ordering together while grid construction remains in NeighborGrid.cpp.

The neighborhood contract validator keeps candidate selection, typed record parsing, rebuild policy, and cross-scenario invariants together; its allocations and branches only construct validation diagnostics and are covered by neighborhood_evidence_test.py.

The neighborhood evidence runner keeps executable discovery, external artifact publication, and strict matrix qualification in one evidence boundary; its branches distinguish contract, process, and record failures and are covered by neighborhood_evidence_test.py.

The delta facade keeps payload-shape, bounded-buffer, stream, checksum, and transactional commit checks at one snapshot boundary; payload serialization and run parsing remain isolated in SnapshotDeltaPayload and SnapshotDeltaStream.

The delta evidence runner keeps versioned contract validation, typed record checks, and external runtime publication together so compression and latency claims cannot bypass fallback, determinism, or transactional checks.

The block-time test entrypoint owns the three-workload matrix and rejects candidate promotion from one visible qualification boundary; schedule mechanics and record validation remain in separate units.

The qualification unit keeps fixed-versus-block event ledgers, migration-boundary checks, restart replay, rollback replay, and input non-mutation together because they form one bounded scheduler contract; it does not implement production forces.

The validator keeps the versioned block-time schema, typed record parsing, and cross-workload invariants at one evidence boundary; allocations are limited to validation diagnostics and no runtime simulation state is owned here.

The test-only BVH index keeps deterministic AABB construction, bottom-up refit, iterative traversal, and topology hashing together because they form one bounded candidate implementation; allocations belong to qualification storage and no production gravity ownership is introduced.

The BVH benchmark keeps refit/rebuild scheduling, exact-reference comparison, selected cell-linked comparison, and separate Octree metrics in one qualification boundary so the promotion decision is based on one coherent workload matrix.

The BVH runner owns the visible record schema and rejects any result that is non-deterministic, non-parity, or selected; it prints only bounded local-query evidence and does not expose a production solver path.

The BVH contract validator keeps typed record parsing, rebuild/refit invariants, exact-neighbor hashes, and the non-promotion policy together at one evidence boundary; allocations only construct diagnostics and parsed records.

The grid layout unit keeps bounded dimension validation, z-major indexing, clamped cell location, and interpolation coordinates together because they are one immutable coordinate contract consumed by deposition and field interpolation.

The grid resource unit keeps view generation, bounded source preparation, CIC deposition, Green convolution, and trilinear interpolation together as one owned storage lifecycle; solver composition and public configuration remain outside the resource.

The TreePM composition root keeps construction, resource rebinding, capacity preparation, and component access together because it owns the lifecycle of the injected PM and Barnes-Hut solvers without duplicating either algorithm.

The TreePM force unit keeps request validation, typed PM and tree evaluation, weighted staging, and transactional force commit together because they form one bounded composition operation with no steady-state allocation.
The PM fixture passes state, execution policy, solver, and three output spans explicitly so the Direct comparison and allocation-free repeatability assertions remain one visible acceptance boundary.

The TreePM fixture passes state, execution policy, solver, and three output spans explicitly so resource ownership, composition repeatability, and Direct comparison remain one visible acceptance boundary.
The PM evidence runner receives output, source root, contract, records, and errors explicitly at the artifact boundary so generated qualification remains external and deterministic.

The restart boundary keeps root-only manifest validation, explicit shard reconstruction, rank-count compatibility, broadcast of restart time, and transactional destination commit together because they form one distributed persistence operation; snapshot codec validation and MPI transport remain delegated.

The metadata parser keeps the single-path and ordered-rank-shard output grammars at the manifest boundary so malformed or reordered shard references cannot enter post-process or restart; filesystem and payload validation remain outside the parser.

The post-process state boundary owns explicit shard reads, stable-ID reconstruction, coverage validation, and metric evaluation as one bounded persistence consumer; allocations are pre-sized for reconstruction and no simulation gather is introduced.

The state-access unit keeps global gather and non-collective local capture beside their shared packet/state validation while preserving separate call contracts; local output is sorted by stable ID and never invokes the distributed gather.

The KIFMM operator unit owns deterministic surface-operator inversion and equivalent-weight construction because those operations share the private workspace and must complete before any force commit; the long numerical kernels are bounded by the fixed surface order.

The KIFMM composition unit keeps settings, resource binding, capacity replacement, request validation, and transactional entrypoint behavior together as the solver lifecycle boundary; surface algebra and traversal are delegated to dedicated units.

The KIFMM traversal unit keeps interaction-list construction, near-field Direct accumulation, far-field equivalent evaluation, and staged target commits together because they form one deterministic tree walk; explicit request objects preserve source and ownership context.

The KIFMM workspace unit owns checked capacity products, fixed surface-node initialization, span access, and transactional growth because these methods define one allocation boundary for all solver-private storage.

The qualification executable keeps the independent Direct/FMM oracle, conservation, repeatability, capacity, singularity, and rollback cases together so one deterministic runtime boundary can qualify KIFMM before public promotion.

The simulation configuration boundary keeps solver construction, candidate rebuild, and resource-setting transactionality together so the newly public KIFMM variant follows the same commit policy as the existing solver families.
